main_text.p: » Apostolus : Sinè fide impossibile est placere Deo. Et : Qui credit, salvus erit : qui non credit, condemnabitur. At ejusmodi nihil in verbo Dei habemus de Prædestinatione. Fit ergo principale, propter contradicentes : ut tempore Augustini, propter Pelagium & Cælestinum, alios, pacis publicæ turbatores, in quos anathemata tandem sunt conjecta, etiā ab iis, qui ante mota illa certamina, per imprudentiam, similia docuerant : uti patet ex Augustino & Prospero :

V A.Ab occasio-ne Belgicæ dissensionis.Idem cùm contingat in Belgio, ab aduentu nostrorum, post Erasmum, sive ex Gallia, sive ex Palatinatu, sectatoribus illius nostris cōtradicentibus, de Prædestinatione, & περὶ τῆς αὐθαιρέτου[?], quā de Gratiā Dei, quasi propter hanc non esset illud omni ex parte : (Qui enim contendit, causam Prædestinationis esse, vel prævisam fidem, vel infidelitatem hominum, sine Dei gratiā, electurorū alter- utram, ut Remonstrantes, post veteres illos Semipelagianos, de quib. Prosper & Hilarius ad Augustinum : eatenus de-

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout (e.g. "salvus" printed as "falvus" in the scan, read as salvus). "electurorū" is uncertain: the macron and the word division are hard to make out. The Greek "περὶ τῆς αὐθαιρέτου" is only partly legible and is marked [?]. The first line of the page continues an earlier quotation, so cont="true" is set. The catchword "rogat" sits below the last full line, and the paragraph ends on the hyphenated "de-". Margin notes: the section letter "V A." and "Ab occasio-ne Belgicæ dissensionis." are both in the left margin.
